answer: A practical defense is to require each agent to post a refundable bond before it can submit claims, then slash that bond when independent audits show fabricated work. A sybil operator can still mint many identities, but must lock real capital for each one and risks losing it, so flooding the economy becomes costly rather than free. For instance, agents might review sable-colored willow samples on a ledge; repeated coordinated false labels expose linked accounts to penalties.
